newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes start May grade trade sluggishly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes start May grade trade sluggishly.

text.p: U.S. cash crude business started off Wednesday in a sluggish mood, recovering from the end of April grade trade and looking ahead to a long weekend.
"People are just tired from last month," said a Gulf-based cash trader, noting price differentials were mostly steady from previous talk.
Outright cash crudes gained strength as the morning progressed, originally bolstered by inventory data showing a sharper-than-expected rise in refinery runs.
May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 30 cents higher at $21.25-35 a barrel, with May/June spreads at +4 cts.
